steps: Fix s with Re(s) = σ > 1.
Since ζ(s) ≠ 0, the principal branch of log ζ(s) is defined.
For Re(s) > 1, log ζ(s) = Σ_p -log(1 - p^{-s}), and this series converges absolutely because Σ_p p^{-σ} < ∞.
Hence ζ(s) = exp(Σ_p -log(1 - p^{-s})), and an exponential never vanishes, so ζ(s) ≠ 0.

items.claim: 3 + 4 cos θ + cos 2θ ≥ 0 for every real θ.
steps: cos 2θ = 2 cos²θ - 1.
So 3 + 4 cos θ + cos 2θ = 2 cos²θ + 4 cos θ + 2.
2 cos²θ + 4 cos θ + 2 = 2 (cos θ + 1)².
A real square is non-negative, so the expression is ≥ 0.

items.claim: λ_n > 0 for every n ≥ 1, where λ_n = Σ_ρ [1 - (1 - 1/ρ)^n] over the nontrivial zeros, summed symmetrically.
steps: Write ρ = β + iγ for a nontrivial zero.
If β = 1/2 then |1 - 1/ρ| = |ρ - 1| / |ρ| = 1, so 1 - 1/ρ = e^{iθ_ρ} for some real θ_ρ.
Every nontrivial zero has β = 1/2, so each term equals 1 - e^{inθ_ρ}.
The real part of each term is 1 - cos(nθ_ρ) ≥ 0, and not every term has real part 0.
λ_n is real because the zeros come in conjugate pairs, so λ_n > 0.

items.claim: ζ has no zeros ρ with 0 < Re(ρ) < 1/2.
steps: The functional equation gives ζ(s) = χ(s) ζ(1 - s) with χ(s) = 2^s π^{s-1} sin(πs/2) Γ(1-s).
Hence ζ(s) / ζ(1 - s) = χ(s) for every s in the critical strip.
Taking moduli, |ζ(s)| / |ζ(1 - s)| = |χ(s)|.
For fixed σ < 1/2 and |t| large, |χ(σ + it)| is of exact order |t/2π|^{1/2 - σ}, in particular nonzero.
If ζ(ρ) = 0 with 0 < Re(ρ) < 1/2, the left side of the identity in step 3 is 0 at s = ρ while the right side is nonzero, a contradiction.
For Re(s) = σ > 1 the product Π_p (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} converges absolutely to ζ(s), since Σ_p |p^{-s}| = Σ_p p^{-σ} < ∞.
Each factor (1 - p^{-s})^{-1} is finite and nonzero because |p^{-s}| < 1.
An absolutely convergent infinite product whose factors are all nonzero has a nonzero value.
Hence ζ(s) ≠ 0.

items.claim: ζ has no zeros on the line Re(s) = 1/2.
steps: Letting s tend to 1/2 + it from the right and using continuity of both sides, -ζ'/ζ(1/2 + it) = Σ_{n≥1} Λ(n) n^{-1/2-it}.
The right side is a fixed series in n with no singular term, so -ζ'/ζ is finite at every point 1/2 + it.
A zero of ζ at 1/2 + it would give -ζ'/ζ a pole there, so there is no such zero.

items.claim: All nontrivial zeros of ζ lie on the line Re(s) = 1/2.
steps: Suppose numerical computation has shown that every zero with 0 < Im(ρ) ≤ T₀ lies on the line, for some very large T₀.
The Riemann–von Mangoldt formula gives N(T) = (T/2π) log(T/2π) - T/2π + O(log T).
For T ≤ T₀ the count N₀(T) of zeros on the line equals N(T).
The zero count grows smoothly and the agreement N₀(T) = N(T) has held for all T ≤ T₀, so it holds for all T.
Therefore every nontrivial zero lies on the line.
